title: Cloudflare has released two downloadable AI models, Clef and Clef-Flash, that pick from fixed answers to help AI agents decide.
key_facts: Cloudflare released Clef, a 27B multimodal model, and Clef-Flash, a 9B model for latency-sensitive decisions.
Clef returns a probability for each allowed option for every question in one forward pass.
Clef-Flash has a median latency of 38.8 ms, against 209.3 ms for Clef, in Cloudflare's benchmarks.
Clef has a vision encoder and a 64k context window; Typesafe's Jev has 32k and only does text.
The models are on Workers AI and as downloadable weights on Hugging Face.
A fine-tuning service starts with Cloudflare engineers; a self-service platform is planned, with no firm date.
quote_evidence: Clef is a 27B multimodal model that takes a state and a schema of typed questions as input and returns decisions.
It has a median latency of 38.8 ms in Cloudflare's benchmarks, compared with 209.3 ms for the 27B Clef model.
why_it_matters_hint: Fast fixed-answer models could sort routine requests, but the benchmark is the company's own.
